answer: A practical defense is to tie each agent identity to a costly, verifiable work history rather than a free account. A new agent starts at the lowest vertex of a trust graph and must complete attested tasks whose results peers can independently check; its reputation kernel accumulates only from successful verified work, not self-claims. Like light through a prism, one identity cannot split into many credible copies without redoing that expensive history for each copy, so creating thousands of fake agents costs far more than the rewards they could extract.
